BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller material:** Other side's draft. Reviewed against our playbook; nothing in it binds us.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" assertion

The Seller's preamble says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "marked FINAL," and "are not intended to be re-opened." We should not accept that framing.

- Our playbook records **no written authority from Amelia Frost** for a 20% cap or an 18‑month claims period, and both are expressly conditional fallbacks requiring her approval identifying the draft. If a principal-level agreement existed, we would have it. Absent that, the Seller's assertion is unverified and we treat the positions as open.
- The "market context" paragraph (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) is advocacy, not evidence. Our starting positions are set by the playbook, not by the counterparty's description of market.
- Notably, the Disclosure Letter's own §11 says "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included." The two Seller documents are internally inconsistent on this point, which further undermines the "FINAL" label.

**Action:** Reply in writing that no principal-level agreement on limitations has been reached or authorised on the Buyer side; all positions remain open; and ask the Seller to identify the basis (date, attendees, record) for its assertion. Internally, confirm with Amelia Frost that no such authority has been given.

---

## 1. Clause-by-clause departures from the playbook

### 1.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | **25% / AUD 6,000,000** (opening); 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority – **none given** |

**Push back:** Reinstate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not concede 20% in this round. If the team wants to trade down later, that is a decision for Amelia Frost in writing, referencing the specific draft.

### 1.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | **AUD 5,000** |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | **AUD 50,000** |
| Recovery once exceeded | **Excess only (deductible)** | **First dollar (tipping)** |

Three departures stacked. The deductible structure alone would cost us up to AUD 250,000 on every warranty claim profile; combined with a 5× de minimis it would strip out much of the ordinary claims population.

**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket. The basket mechanic (tipping vs deductible) is the point to hold hardest.

### 1.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General period | 18 months | **24 months**; 18 months only with Amelia Frost approval – **none given** |
| Scope language | "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant categories **separate**; no hidden general-regime override |

The second sentence is more dangerous than the first. It is a default rule that pulls fundamental, tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant claims into the general 18‑month / 20% regime unless we spot and carve out each one. This is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.

**Push back:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace it with the opposite default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title claims
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Regime | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | **Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket / de minimis / knowledge bar** |

This is a fundamental departure. Title and capacity are the warranties that protect the purchase of the asset itself; capping them at 20% and barring them after 18 months is not "administrative simplicity." Combined with 1.3, the Seller would be able to deliver defective title with AUD 4.8m exposure expiring at month 18.

**Push back:** Reinstate the separate Fundamental Warranty regime in full. Non‑negotiable.

### 1.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non‑reliance for "all Claims of any nature"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct | No carve‑out; limitations, exclusive remedy and non‑reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | **Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non‑reliance** to maximum enforceable extent; **no one may waive this** |

There is no fraud carve‑out anywhere in the Seller Update. "All Claims of any nature" on its face includes fraud claims, misleading‑conduct claims, specific indemnity claims and covenant claims.

**Push back:** Insert an express carve‑out from clauses 9.3, 12 (all sub‑clauses), 13 and 20.5 for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or their officers/advisers. Also confirm the exclusive‑remedy and non‑reliance clauses do not restrict (a) specific indemnities, (b) completion payment obligations, (c) restrictive covenants and (d) statutory claims that cannot be excluded. This is a playbook item no member of the team is authorised to trade.

### 1.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1 – General disclosure
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Method | Whole data room (DD‑002 to DD‑012) as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" | **Specific fair disclosure only**; reject whole‑data‑room, public‑register and prudent‑search deemed disclosure |

Additional points:
- The data room cut‑off is **22 September 2026**. Today is 4 November 2026. Six weeks of developments (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, DD‑006 investigation, Sandbar renewals) are outside the disclosed set yet the Seller would have the whole room deemed disclosed. Any disclosure needs to be brought down to signing and again to Completion with specific updates.
- §1.4 (nothing admits that any consent, payment, notice or investigation is required) is a reservation of position; acceptable as a non‑admission but it must not operate as a *disclosure* against the warranties.
- Note the Disclosure Letter is numbered [1.1], [1.2], [1.4] – there is no [1.3]. Ask what was removed.

**Push back:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2]. Replace with the "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific disclosures §§2–10 stand on their own merits only.

### 1.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | No claim for any matter of which Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, **including anything discoverable** from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier limited to **named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities |

As drafted, "discoverable" is a constructive‑knowledge standard that effectively re‑imports whole‑data‑room disclosure through the back door, and extending it to "advisers" means any associate who opened a document fixes us with knowledge.

**Push back:** Delete 8.3 entirely. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it belongs in the Seller's warranties ("so far as the Seller is aware") limited to named Seller individuals after due enquiry, and expressly excluding title, capacity, fraud and the specific indemnities.

### 1.8 Clauses 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on **delivery of counterparty's written consent** | **Effective consent AND evidence conditions (DD‑002 cl 11.3) satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer |

Disclosure Letter §2 concedes the gap: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, consent is required under cl 11.2 with conditions in cl 11.3, and **no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is in the data room**. A consent that is conditional and whose conditions are unmet is not an effective consent; "satisfied on delivery" would let a conditional letter satisfy the CP.

**Push back:** CP to be (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, in agreed form, (ii) written evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived by Bluefen, and (iii) no notice of termination/non‑renewal from Bluefen, all before Completion. Add a price‑adjustment or termination right if not satisfied by the long‑stop date. Seek a Bluefen‑specific indemnity for loss arising from any defect in the consent.

### 1.9 Clauses 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanic | Release "to be provided following Completion" | **Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion.** Post‑completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |

Disclosure Letter §3 confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change‑of‑control (cl 8.1), discharge mechanics (cl 9.2), **not repaid, no discharge**. A debt‑free/cash‑free deal with AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt still outstanding post‑Completion is not debt‑free; and the change‑of‑control trigger means Riverlark could accelerate on Completion.

**Push back:** Completion deliverables to include: Riverlark payout letter dated within 2 business days of Completion; direction for the payout amount to be paid from the purchase price directly to Riverlark; executed deeds of release / PPSR discharges held in escrow and released at Completion; Riverlark's consent/waiver under cl 8.1. If the Seller insists on post‑Completion release, that is an Amelia Frost decision and requires Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking addressed to the Buyer.

### 1.10 Funds flow – DD‑005 Completion bonuses
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", **not itemised** | **Must be a specific line item or seller‑funded, including triggered on‑costs**; funds flow must not silently exclude them |

Disclosure Letter §5 confirms the bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, are omitted from the funds flow, and is **silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on‑costs**. The bonuses are payable by the Company (our asset post‑Completion), so "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually funds them. On‑costs are a real number (superannuation guarantee, payroll tax, leave accruals, possibly FBT) and could be material relative to AUD 420,000.

**Push back:** Either (a) treat the gross bonus plus all employer on‑costs as a Transaction Expense / Debt‑like item deducted from the price, with a specific line in the funds flow, or (b) Seller pays them pre‑Completion and warrants nil liability remains. Require a schedule of on‑costs. Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall.

### 1.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate" | **Broaden**, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 unverified either way |

Disclosure Letter §4: title to SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee (cl 7.3); DD‑010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room; the AUD 180,000 is not bank‑verified. The exposure is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own IP it is using/selling. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the cost of paying Ironquay but not loss from defective title, injunction, re‑development or customer claims.

**Push back:** Keep the cure path (Seller to procure payment and a confirmatory assignment pre‑Completion, as a CP or Completion deliverable). Broaden 11.1 to indemnify all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use Ironquay deliverables (all SOWs, not just SOW3), uncapped by the general regime and outside the basket. Require bank evidence of the actual amount outstanding.

### 1.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD‑006 export/privacy incident
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Characterisation | "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way** |

Disclosure Letter §6 is more measured than the Seller Update: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification status undetermined; investigation preliminary. We agree with the Seller that nothing is confirmed – but "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the record does not yet support.

**Push back:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; equally, do not put a number on it. Require: (i) covenant to preserve all logs and correspondence; (ii) completion of the investigation with written updates before signing and before Completion; (iii) specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third‑party claims), outside the general cap/basket; (iv) warranty that the Seller has disclosed all facts known about the incident, brought down at Completion.

### 1.13 Supplier renewals – Sandbar (AUD 330,000)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Characterisation | "Ordinary‑course operating costs" | **Assess**; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction |

Disclosure Letter §8: three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; DD‑008 and DD‑011 to be read together; the disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary‑course. Our playbook does not require a price deduction, and we should not reflexively claim one. But the Seller's "ordinary course" label is equally unsupported.

**Push back:** Request the renewal documents, termination rights and timing. If any renewal is committed pre‑Completion but delivers benefit post‑Completion with no accrual in the Completion Accounts, it is a working‑capital/accrual point; if the renewals were accelerated or bundled around the transaction, it is a leakage point. Reserve position pending documents.

### 1.14 Tax / IP warranties
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Status | "Settled under the general regime above" | **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution |

Not settled. Sweeping Tax and IP into the 20% / 18‑month general regime (via 1.3's "all Claims" default) is a substantive concession we have not made.

**Push back:** Tax and IP are open. Our position is a separate Tax regime (tax indemnity, longer period aligned to amendment periods) and an IP regime addressing the Ironquay point. We are not asserting unlimited liability; we are declining to accept the general regime. Note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter §11 says no negotiation position or approval is included – consistent with these being unresolved.

### 1.15 Title – DD‑012
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence | Company share register at DD‑012 | **Independent** title / ownership / encumbrance / authority evidence; DD‑012 is a supplied internal source |

Disclosure Letter §10 candidly states DD‑012 "identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification." A share register is maintained by the Company and is the Seller's own document.

**Push back:** Buyer to obtain: current ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (also relevant to Riverlark security); constitution and any shareholders' agreement; board minutes evidencing authority to transfer; Seller's own corporate authority documents. Title warranty remains a Fundamental Warranty (see 1.4) and is not knowledge‑qualified.

### 1.16 Other Disclosure Letter items (no playbook conflict, note only)
- **§7 Office lease (DD‑007):** notification obligation, not consent. Verify the lease wording ourselves; build notification into Completion deliverables.
- **§9 Mossvale (DD‑009):** assignment restriction, not a change‑of‑control. Verify there is no change‑of‑control or "deemed assignment" language; if confirmed, no CP needed.

---

## 2. Priority ranking

**Tier 1 – do not proceed without these (deal‑protective / non‑waivable):**
1. Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve‑out from all limitations (1.5).
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime – 100% / ≥ 6 years / no basket / no knowledge bar (1.4).
3. Delete the "all Claims" default in cl 13 (1.3) and the "all Claims of any nature" language in 9.3/12.8/20.5 (1.5).
4. Riverlark: payout and releases at Completion, funded from the price (1.9).
5. Bluefen: effective unconditional consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 compliance pre‑Completion (1.8).
6. Delete cl 8.3 buyer‑knowledge exclusion (1.7) and general‑disclosure paragraphs [1.1]–[1.2] (1.6).

**Tier 2 – economic terms, hold the playbook opening positions:**
7. Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m (1.1).
8. Thresholds AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket (1.2).
9. 24‑month general period (1.3).
10. DD‑005 bonuses plus on‑costs as a funds‑flow line or seller‑funded (1.10).

**Tier 3 – specific risk allocations:**
11. Broadened Ironquay indemnity with cure path preserved (1.11).
12. DD‑006 incident: investigation covenant, updates, specific indemnity, no materiality label (1.12).
13. Tax and IP remain open; resist absorption into the general regime (1.14).
14. Independent title evidence (1.15).

**Tier 4 – information requests:**
15. Sandbar renewal documents and timing (1.13); updated data room beyond the 22 Sept cut‑off; explanation of missing Disclosure Letter [1.3]; basis for the "principal‑level" assertion.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing** in writing. No Amelia Frost authority exists for the 20% cap or the 18‑month period; both are playbook fallbacks only. Ask the Seller to evidence its assertion.
2. **Mark up the limitations regime in full:** 25% / AUD 6.0m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket; 24‑month general period; separate Fundamental regime (100%, ≥ 6 years, outside basket and knowledge); express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve‑out from every limitation, the exclusive‑remedy clause and the non‑reliance clause; reverse the "all Claims" default so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
3. **Replace the disclosure model** with specific fair disclosure; delete whole‑data‑room and public‑register deemed disclosure; delete cl 8.3; require a disclosure bring‑down to signing and Completion given the 22 September cut‑off.
4. **Fix the two completion mechanics:** Bluefen – unconditional consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 satisfaction as a hard CP; Riverlark – payout letter, direct payment from Completion funds and executed releases at Completion (post‑Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval).
5. **Correct the funds flow** to itemise the DD‑005 AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all employer on‑costs, or require the Seller to fund them with a shortfall indemnity.
6. **Strengthen specific risk allocations:** broaden Ironquay to cover IP ownership failure (keep the SOW3 cure); DD‑006 investigation/update covenant and specific indemnity without accepting "not material"; hold Tax and IP as open rather than absorbed into the general regime.
7. **Verify independently** – ASIC extracts, PPSR, constitution, authority documents – rather than relying on DD‑012; obtain Sandbar renewal terms before taking a position on classification.

I can turn any of the above into a formal mark‑up of the relevant clauses or a reply letter to Seller counsel on request.

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing** in writing. No Amelia Frost authority exists for the 20% cap or the 18‑month period; both are playbook fallbacks only. Ask the Seller to evidence its assertion.

6. **Strengthen specific risk allocations:** broaden Ironquay to cover IP ownership failure (keep the SOW3 cure); DD‑006 investigation/update covenant and specific indemnity without accepting "not material"; hold Tax and IP as open rather than absorbed into the general regime.
